canonical_answers: Solving L dI/dt+RI=ℰ gives I=(ℰ/R)(1-e^{-Rt/L}) and time constant L/R.

payload.text: An LR circuit with inductance L and resistance R is connected to constant emf ℰ at t=0 with I(0)=0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: A valid design varies the inductance L as the independent variable, measures the resulting time constant τ=L/R (from the current growth curve) as the dependent variable, and holds the resistance R and emf ℰ constant as controls, consistent with I=(ℰ/R)(1-e^{-Rt/L}).
required_evidence: dependent variable: measured time constant τ=L/R
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, explicitly show independent variable: inductance L; dependent variable: measured time constant τ=L/R; control: constant R and ℰ.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State the governing principle (Kirchhoff's voltage law) and the initial-condition assumption I(0)=0, and explain why each must hold for the proposed measurement of the time constant L/R to be valid.

criteria.description: State the governing principle (Kirchhoff's voltage law) and the initial-condition assumption I(0)=0, and explain why each must hold for the proposed measurement of the time constant L/R to be valid.
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
criteria.minimum_fix: To earn this point, state Kirchhoff's voltage law as the governing principle and I(0)=0 as the initial condition, and explain that both must hold for the measured current growth to isolate the L/R time constant.

accessibility.accommodation_notes: Text and symbolic notation are fully described.
